frame_metadata.gps_note: Every frame carries capture time with a -04:00 offset and the F0 build's 9-key GPS block. But from the first label (f0004, 16:18) to the exterior (f0028, 16:33) every frame carries the same fix, taken at 16:16:20 by the entrance: the phone produced no new fix indoors. The fix places the take at Cooper Hewitt; it says nothing about where in the building a frame was shot.

differ.medium: label 'Ink on coated paper', catalog 'screen-printed on paper' — a technique against a material; not a contradiction, two different descriptions

related_groups.g0005: The extended caption below this label ('Popular in the 18th century, toiles de Jouy…'), shot as a label group with the same wallpaper as its work. Tester's note: 'Duplicate of Harlem Toile de Jouy wallpaper'. It has no tombstone and no number (accession 'unread' twice), so it is not a fixture of its own; its frames are kept here. f0015 is the same caption shot as wall text.

traps.date_shaped_accession: The number reads as a date, and the tester answered 'no number' on the spot. Cooper Hewitt's key is acquisition year, lot, item. See data/venues/cooper-hewitt.json traps.
traps.ocr_of_the_work: Vision read the wallpaper's own edge printing as '7.' and 'n Tolle' / 'Tolle' above the title — text in the work, not on the label.
